chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: More of Fletcher Henderson's 1940 personnel
summary: Collins adds George Irish, Freddy Mitchell, Rudy Powell and Peanuts Holland to the band he remembers.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You were talking about the personnel of Fletcher Henderson's band when you were in it, and you got as far as Joe Keys, Pops Smith, Jonah Jones, trumpet, and you mentioned Clyde Jones, Sandy Williams on trombone. And then later you mentioned Walter Johnson on drums. Who else can you remember?

Well, now, George Irish, a very fine tenor player from Boston, who's with us. Freddy Mitchell, who's another very good tenor player from New York, and Rudy Powell, alto. Everybody knows Rudy. He was with everybody. He was with Teddy Wilson's band, a very good band, when Ben was there, and J. C. And George Dorsey was alto, and Ted Sturges a bass Bates, and I don't know how I could have forgot Peanuts Holland. He was playing trumpet then, a very fine trumpet player. He was one of the giants, you know.
So that was -- most of the band that I can remember at this point.
